newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen in "lousy" bounce.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. stocks seen in "lousy" bounce.

text.p: The rally on Monday in U.S. blue chips that brought the second-biggest point gain in the history of the Dow Jones Industrial Average did not have the broad support to indicate an end to Wall Street's woes.

Technical analysts on Tuesday said the Dow will face stiff resistance at the 6750-to-6800 Dow level and may break below its recent low point at 6350. The Dow was up 12 at 6599 in afternoon trading on Wednesday.
"It's going to be a lousy bounce," said John Wosczyna market strategist at Roney & Co.
"If you look at two-and-a-half or three months (and) you only go up 300 or 400 (Dow) points, that's not much in this volatile market," Wosczyna added.
On Monday the Dow industrials leaped 134 points after market-friendly inflation data and solid quarterly earnings.
The surge trailed only the 187-point jump two days after 1987's Black Monday crash among top point rises in Dow history. In percentage terms, however, Monday's rise was not among the top gainers.
Before the rally, Dow had fallen 9.8 percent off its record closing high set on March 11 at 7085.
But despite the Dow's fireworks, technical analysts said they were unimpressed by Monday's action.
While advancing issues beat decliners by a two-to-one ratio on the New York Stock Exchange, the breadth was not runaway positive, they said.
More importantly, they noted the lack of support from braod sectors of stocks. The Nasdaq composite fell 3.5 points on Monday and was off nine points Tuesday afternoon at 1204.
"The evidence leans more toward the idea that the correction has further to go," said Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
Monday's rally may have established 6400 or 6350 as a near-term Dow low point. But the base is not solid enough to indicate a major renewed rally, said Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities.

Stocks will likely be locked in a choppy trading range characterized by quick investor moves in and out of stock groups. "We'll see a lot of rotation," he said. "Things bubble up to the top and then three weeks later they've sunk right back to the middle."
The Dow 6350 mark has taken shape as a key downside level for stocks, the technicians said.
"Any close below 6350 would be quite negative and probably lead to a move on down toward the 6000s," Harrington said. He said he expected 6350 to break over the coming weeks.
Wosczyna said he was convinced U.S. stocks were in the grip of a bear market. He said he expected stocks to fall between 25 and 30 percent off their peaks in eight to 15 months.
That would drop the Dow to between 5000 and 5300.
